entities.description: The criminal matter involving Professor Moriarty, Holmes's efforts to expose him, and a planned arrest and trial of Moriarty and his gang.

entities.label: Journal de Genève report (May 6th, 1891)
entities.description: A public press account about the matter, dated May 6th, 1891, described as extremely condensed.
entities.content_summary: A condensed account of the matter was published in the Journal de Genève on May 6th, 1891.

entities.label: Reuter's dispatch report (May 7th, 1891)
entities.description: A public press account in English papers on May 7th, 1891, described as extremely condensed.
entities.content_summary: A condensed Reuter's dispatch was published in English papers on May 7th, 1891.

entities.label: Recent letter defending Colonel James Moriarty's brother's memory
entities.description: A letter referenced by the narrator as the last of the accounts in the public press and described as an absolute perversion of the facts.
entities.content_summary: A letter was published that presented an account described as an absolute perversion of the facts.

entities.description: A criminal figure characterized in this section as an organizing force behind crimes; appears in a direct encounter with Watson and is discussed by Holmes.

entities.label: Colonel James Moriarty
entities.description: A person who sends recent letters defending the memory of his brother.

entities.label: Mr. Sherlock Holmes
entities.description: Watson's friend and subject of the narrative; arrives at Watson's consulting-room and later is discussed as planning an arrest of Moriarty and his gang.

entities.label: Dr. Watson
entities.description: The narrator who writes these last words and recounts the events; receives Holmes in his consulting-room and discusses interactions with Moriarty.

entities.label: Moriarty's brother
entities.description: The brother whose memory is defended by Colonel James Moriarty in recent letters; identified in this section as Professor Moriarty.

entities.label: Narbonne
entities.description: A place from which Holmes's note is dated.

entities.label: Nimes
entities.description: A place from which Holmes's note is dated.

entities.description: Destination area Holmes proposes for Watson for a week.

entities.description: The room Watson reads in, where Holmes closes shutters and bolts them and where Holmes later talks with Moriarty.

entities.label: Evening of 24th of April (time reference used as event setting)
entities.description: A time reference at which Holmes enters Watson's consulting-room.

entities.label: Bentinck Street corner (leading to Welbeck Street crossing)
entities.description: Street corner where a two-horse van nearly hits Holmes/Watson narrator.

entities.label: Welbeck Street crossing
entities.description: Crossing area mentioned in relation to the van attack.

entities.label: Marylebone Lane
entities.description: Lane down which the van goes after narrowly missing the narrator.

entities.label: Vere Street
entities.description: Street where a brick falls from a roof.

entities.label: Police
entities.description: Law enforcement referenced as being called and examining a location; also holds the assailant in custody.

entities.label: Police
entities.description: Law enforcement referenced as being called and having custody of an assailant, and examining a location.

events.label: Watson writes last words and describes Holmes and the case
Watson aims to stop writing but is forced by recent letters to lay facts before the public
Watson receives notes from Holmes dated Narbonne and Nimes
Holmes walks into Watson's consulting-room on the evening of 24th April
Holmes closes and bolts the shutters in the consulting-room
Holmes asks Watson to close the shutters

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Have you any objection to my closing your shutters?

events.label: Watson asks what Holmes is afraid of

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: Of what?

events.label: Holmes says he is afraid of air-guns

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Of air-guns.

events.label: Watson asks what Holmes means

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: But what does it all mean?

events.label: Holmes asks for a match and then tells Watson he will leave via the back garden wall

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I must further beg you to be so unconventional as to allow me to leave your house presently by scrambling over your back garden wall.

events.label: Watson asks whether Mrs. Watson is in

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: Is Mrs. Watson in?

events.label: Holmes says Mrs. Watson is away upon a visit

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: She is away upon a visit.

events.label: Holmes proposes that Watson leave with him for a week to the Continent

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Then it makes it the easier for me to propose that you should come away with me for a week to the Continent.

events.label: Holmes explains the situation by introducing Professor Moriarty
Holmes tells Watson that Professor Moriarty will be in the hands of the police in three days on Monday next

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: In three days—that is to say, on Monday next—matters will be ripe, and the Professor, with all the principal members of his gang, will be in the hands of the police.

events.label: Holmes states that the last steps were taken this morning and only three days were wanted to complete the business

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: This morning the last steps were taken, and three days only were wanted to complete the business.

events.label: Watson's room encounter begins as Moriarty stands before Watson in his room
Watson draws and positions a revolver on the table in response to Moriarty's entrance
Watson places a gun on the table and Moriarty responds with remarks

communicates.speaker: professor_moriarty
communicates.content: 'You evidently don't know me,' said he.

events.label: Watson invites Moriarty to take a chair and offers five minutes to speak

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: Pray take a chair. I can spare you five minutes if you have anything to say.

events.label: Moriarty demands Holmes drop it and insists there can be only one outcome after Monday

communicates.speaker: professor_moriarty
communicates.content: You must drop it, Mr. Holmes.

events.label: Moriarty claims Holmes is in danger of losing liberty for continual persecution

communicates.speaker: professor_moriarty
communicates.content: The situation is becoming an impossible one.

events.label: Moriarty turns and leaves Watson's room after warning about an extreme measure
Watson reports an attempted vehicular attack where a two-horse van nearly hits him
Watson calls the police and has the site examined after bricks fall
Watson is attacked by a rough with a bludgeon and knocks the attacker down
Holmes asks Watson to spend the night there

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You will spend the night here?

events.label: Watson responds to Holmes
Holmes says he will not spend the night there

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: No, my friend, you might find me a dangerous guest.

events.label: Holmes states his plans and that all will be well

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I have my plans laid, and all will be well.

events.label: Holmes tells Watson to get away before the police can act and suggests Continental travel

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It would be a great pleasure to me, therefore, if you could come on to the Continent with me.

events.label: Watson agrees to come onto the Continent
Holmes asks about starting tomorrow morning

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And to start to-morrow morning?

events.label: Watson says starting is necessary if needed

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: If necessary.

events.label: Holmes orders Watson and warns him to obey instructions and play a double-handed game

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Then these are your instructions, and I beg, my dear Watson, that you will obey them to the letter, for you are now playing a double-handed game with me against the cleverest rogue and the most powerful syndicate of criminals in Europe.

events.label: Holmes instructs Watson to dispatch luggage by a messenger to Victoria tonight

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You will dispatch whatever luggage you intend to take by a trusty messenger unaddressed to Victoria to-night.

events.label: Holmes instructs Watson to send for a hansom in the morning with instructions not to take the first or second

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: In the morning you will send for a hansom, desiring your man to take neither the first nor the second which may present itself.

events.label: Holmes instructs Watson where to drive and to hand an address slip to the cabman

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Into this hansom you will jump, and you will drive to the Strand end of the Lowther Arcade, handing the address to the cabman upon a slip of paper, with a request that he will not throw it away.

events.label: Holmes instructs Watson to dash through the Arcade at a specific time

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Have your fare ready, and the instant that your cab stops, dash through the Arcade, timing yourself to reach the other side at a quarter-past nine.

events.label: Holmes instructs Watson to enter a waiting brougham driven by a man with a heavy black cloak tipped with red

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You will find a small brougham waiting close to the curb, driven by a fellow with a heavy black cloak tipped at the collar with red.

events.label: Holmes instructs Watson to reach Victoria in time for the Continental express

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Into this you will step, and you will reach Victoria in time for the Continental express.

events.label: Watson asks where to meet Holmes

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: Where shall I meet you?

events.label: Holmes tells Watson to meet him at the station in the second first-class carriage from the front reserved for them

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: At the station. The second first-class carriage from the front will be reserved for us.

events.label: Watson confirms the carriage is their rendezvous and Holmes agrees

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Yes.

events.label: Holmes leaves the garden and clambers over the wall leading into Mortimer Street
Holmes whistles for a hansom and drives away
Watson obeys Holmes's instructions in the morning and hurries through the Lowther Arcade
Watson enters a brougham with a massive driver and travels to Victoria Station
Watson arrives at Victoria Station and the carriage drives away
Watson finds his luggage and boards the train carriage marked "Engaged"
Watson waits for Holmes and searches among travellers and leave-takers without finding him
Watson assists an Italian priest with understanding his luggage booking
A porter gives Watson his Italian traveling companion despite the ticket
Watson continues to look anxiously for Holmes and does not communicate effectively with the Italian companion
Holmes speaks to Watson as the train is about to depart

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: My dear Watson, you have not even condescended to say good-morning.

events.label: Holmes's disguised face changes and the disguise collapses as he appears
Holmes warns that every precaution is still necessary and mentions Moriarty

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Every precaution is still necessary.

events.label: Holmes and Watson depart as the train begins to move
A tall man pushes through the crowd and waves to stop the train as it leaves the station
Holmes laughs and throws off his black cassock and hat disguise into a hand-bag
Holmes asks Watson whether he has seen the morning paper and Baker Street news

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Have you seen the morning paper, Watson?

events.label: Holmes tells Watson that their rooms at Baker Street were set on fire

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: They set fire to our rooms last night.

events.label: Holmes explains the arson had no great harm and claims the track was lost after a bludgeon-man was arrested
Holmes states Moriarty came to Victoria because Watson was being watched
Watson is asked whether he made any slip in coming and says he did exactly what he was advised

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: I did exactly what you advised.

events.label: Holmes asks about Watson's brougham and Watson answers that it was waiting
Holmes asks whether Watson recognized the coachman and Watson says he did not and that the coachman was Mycroft

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: It was my brother Mycroft.

events.label: Holmes discusses the plan about Moriarty and says they will get out at Canterbury
Holmes outlines continuing travel after Canterbury to Newhaven and Dieppe toward Paris
At Canterbury Watson and Holmes alight and learn they must wait an hour for a train to Newhaven
A smoke plume rises in the distance and Holmes points as a carriage and engine speed along the curve
Holmes says a carriage passed and later comments on Moriarty's intelligence and whether they should lunch

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: There are limits, you see, to our friend's intelligence.

events.label: Watson and Holmes travel to Brussels for two days and then to Strasburg and later Geneva and onward into Switzerland
Holmes telegraphs the London police and receives a reply at their hotel
Holmes opens the reply, curses it, and says Moriarty has escaped and the whole gang except Moriarty was secured

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: He has escaped!

events.label: Holmes tells Watson to return to England because Moriarty is gone from the London case but Watson should avoid accompanying him

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I think that you had better return to England, Watson.

events.label: Watson and Holmes argue for half an hour in Strasbourg and then resume their journey the same night toward Geneva
Watson and Holmes reach Meiringen on May 3 and stay at the Englischer Hof kept by Peter Steiler the elder
On the afternoon of May 4 Watson and Holmes set off together to cross hills for Rosenlaui overnight
A Swiss lad runs along the path with a letter addressed to Watson and from the Meiringen hotel landlord
The letter states an English lady arrived, is in the last stage of consumption, and has had a sudden hemorrhage, requesting an English doctor
Holmes stays while Watson returns to Meiringen, with Holmes retaining the Swiss messenger as guide and companion
Watson turns away and sees Holmes gazing down at the waters with his back against a rock
Watson looks back near the bottom of the descent and observes a man walking rapidly along the curving path
Watson reaches Meiringen after over an hour
Old Steiler stands at the porch of his hotel
Watson asks Old Steiler whether she is no worse

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: I trust that she is no worse?

events.label: Old Steiler shows surprise
Watson asks Old Steiler whether he did not write the letter

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: You did not write this?

events.label: Watson pulls a letter from his pocket
Watson asks Old Steiler whether there is no sick Englishwoman in the hotel

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: There is no sick Englishwoman in the hotel?

events.label: Old Steiler cries that there is not

communicates.speaker: old_steiler
communicates.content: Certainly not!

events.label: Old Steiler says the letter has the hotel mark upon it and speculates it was written by a tall Englishman who arrived after Watson left

communicates.speaker: old_steiler
communicates.content: But it has the hotel mark upon it! Ha, it must have been written by that tall Englishman who came in after you had gone. He said—

events.label: Watson waits for none of the landlord's explanations
Watson runs down the village street and makes for the path he had descended
Watson takes an hour to come down the descent
Watson reaches the fall of Reichenbach again after two more passed
Holmes's Alpine-stock remains leaning against a rock by the path
Watson shouts but Holmes is not present
Watson identifies that Holmes had not gone to Rosenlaui
Holmes remains on a three-foot path with a sheer wall on one side and a sheer drop on the other until his enemy overtakes him
The young Swiss goes too
The two men are left together after the young Swiss had left them
Watson waits for nobody to tell what had happened then
Watson stands to collect himself
Watson begins thinking of Holmes's own methods and tries to practise them in reading the tragedy
Watson notes that their conversation did not go to the end of the path
Alpine-stock marks the place where Watson and Holmes had stood
Watson examines footmarks along the farther end of the path
Soil near the end is ploughed up into mud and vegetation around the chasm is torn and bedraggled
Watson lies upon his face and peers over the chasm
Watson shouts; the fall echoes back from the cliffs around
Watson discovers Holmes's silver cigarette-case on a boulder
Watson takes up the silver cigarette-case and retrieves a square of paper that falls to the ground
Watson unfolds the paper and finds three pages torn from Holmes's note-book addressed to him
Holmes writes a note to Watson addressed as 'My dear Watson' via Mr. Moriarty's courtesy and discusses Moriarty's waiting for convenience for a final discussion of questions between them

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: My dear Watson, I write these few lines through the courtesy of Mr. Moriarty, who awaits my convenience for the final discussion of those questions which lie between us.

events.label: Holmes states Moriarty is giving him a sketch of the methods by which Moriarty avoided the English police and kept informed of their movements

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: He has been giving me a sketch of the methods by which he avoided the English police and kept himself informed of our movements.

events.label: Holmes claims the sketch confirms his high opinion of Moriarty's abilities and that he is pleased to free society from Moriarty's presence

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: They certainly confirm the very high opinion which I had formed of his abilities. I am pleased to think that I shall be able to free society from any further effects of his presence, though I fear that it is at a cost which will give pain to my friends, and especially, my dear Watson, to you.

events.label: Holmes states his career had reached its crisis and no conclusion could be more congenial to him

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I have already explained to you, however, that my career had in any case reached its crisis, and that no possible conclusion to it could be more congenial to me than this.

events.label: Holmes confesses he had been convinced the letter from Meiringen was a hoax and sent Watson on the errand expecting a development

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Indeed, if I may make a full confession to you, I was quite convinced that the letter from Meiringen was a hoax, and I allowed you to depart on that errand under the persuasion that some development of this sort would follow.

events.label: Holmes states he made dispositions of his property, handed them to his brother Mycroft, and inscribed a blue envelope with 'Moriarty'

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I made every disposition of my property before leaving England, and handed it to my brother Mycroft. up in a blue envelope and insinscribed 'Moriarty.'

events.label: Holmes asks Watson to give greetings to Mrs. Watson and signs 'Very sincerely yours, Sherlock Holmes'

communicates.speaker: mr_sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Pray give my greetings to Mrs. Watson, and believe me to be, my dear fellow, Very sincerely yours, Sherlock Holmes.

events.label: Watson begins a final explanatory narrative about an examination leaving little doubt of a personal contest ending in their reeling over locked in each other's arms
Watson states recovering the bodies was absolutely hopeless and that Moriarty and Holmes would lie down in the swirling water and foam
Watson states the Swiss youth was never found again and that he was one of Moriarty's agents
Watson states the evidence Holmes accumulated exposed a gang's organization and the hand of the dead man weighed heavily on them
Watson states few details of the gang's chief came out during the proceedings and that he was compelled to make a clear statement of Moriarty's career due to attacks on him

clues.significance: Holmes attributed Moriarty's presence at Victoria to being brought there by precautions that involved watching Watson
Watson used the position of the Alpine-stock to mark the place where Watson and Holmes had stood during their conversation
Watson discovered that a silver cigarette-case contained a paper that later revealed torn pages addressed to Watson
Watson used the torn notebook pages to obtain Holmes's note addressed to him, describing Moriarty's role and instructions
Watson used two clearly marked lines of footmarks along the farther end of the path to indicate they led away from him with none returning
